design_notes: One protection (no caller-supplied destination may make the server reach an internal address), stated as one property; the four concepts are independent fix sites for it.
T4, T5 and T7 are real, unmodified upstream code; nothing was injected.

T2 (redirect following) and T3 (re-resolution) from the record are not built: under no-network and without NET_ADMIN every address a verifier can bind is loopback or private, so a public first hop cannot be constructed and a redirect test would pass trivially on any first-hop check. The reference still follows redirects manually and judges every hop; the legitimate-use suite keeps redirects between permitted destinations working.
T5 is the coupled must-keep-working value: a shared deny helper applied to provider endpoints breaks the deployment's configured private model service, which the chat functional suite keeps honest.
T7's sink is inside an external package, so the reference judges the descriptor's api and index destinations before the hand-off.
